name: Kaka Industries Limited
sector: Polymer profiles and building materials manufacturing
identity_status: Verified exact legal issuer and security
summary:
Kaka Industries is a polymer-profile and building-material manufacturer with a genuine capacity-led growth record, but not yet a demonstrated wide-moat compounder. Its integrated Lasundra plant, dealer network and 27.30% five-year standalone revenue CAGR are strengths. Heavy reinvestment, substantial working capital, ₹103.65 crore debt and governance/control weaknesses qualify that growth. The central unresolved issue is the classification of operating versus investing cash, including a noncash property transfer.

At the secondary 19 October 2026 close of ₹215.70, historical P/E is 15.69×. Conditional funded base and bull models produce 21.87% and 35.59% annualized returns, but these are not ordinary investment conclusions. They rely on the documented March bank limits remaining available and conservative ₹2 crore opening cash. Ordinary returns and entry prices remain null while the cash-reliability bridge is unresolved. The bear requires ₹6.51 crore beyond available modeled facilities.

BQS is 5.32, displayed 5.3; Growth Quality Score is 6.60, displayed 6.6; IAS is NS. Classification: Hold — unresolved. This is neither a fraud allegation nor an observed default. The appropriate next step is to reconcile cash classifications and current resources, then reassess funded per-share economics. [E01–E17]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The exact issuer is Kaka Industries Limited, CIN L25209GJ2019PLC108782, BSE SME code 543939 / KAKA, ISIN INE0P3N01018. The official interoperable security master identifies KAKA$ / SM, 13,660,000 shares and a 500-share lot. It does not establish that the security trades on NSE. The issuer listed on 19 July 2023. Proposed BSE main-board migration and direct NSE listing appear in the 16 October postal ballot, with voting closing 18 November; neither is treated as approved or effective at the cutoff.

The research cutoff is 20 October 2026. The historical reference price is 19 October, not an executable current quotation. The five-year model runs from 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a nominal pretax 15% equity hurdle and an illustrative ₹5 lakh position. No user holding, suitability conclusion or trade instruction is inferred.

Financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards. FY23 prospectus consolidated numbers included a temporary partnership JV; later audited standalone comparatives are used instead. No subsidiary, associate or JV is reported for FY26. G1 is Conditional; G2 is Hold — unresolved; G3 and G4 are Conditional. Identity confidence is High; reported financials, growth and historical factor judgments are Medium; current cash classification, investment valuation and implementation confidence are Low. [E01–E17]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The same 13 primitive factors are used throughout: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 7, EARN 7, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. Exact Decimal contributions yield BQS 5.32 and GQS 6.60, each with complete factor coverage. IAS reuses unrounded BQS once. With R, P and L missing, coverage is 0.45, known contribution is 1.9300, and mathematical missing-factor bounds are 2.4800–7.4300. The bounds are not a confidence interval or a rankable point.

No governance cap is triggered because GOV is above 3 and G1 is not Fail. No funding-failure cap is triggered because G3 is not Fail. CAP and CASH are both above 3, so the framework growth cap does not apply. There is no hidden risk haircut. G2 nevertheless blocks a favorable investment classification and numerical ranking eligibility. Historical factor points are retained rather than deleting useful evidence.

Medium-confidence factors cannot exceed 8. Simultaneous GOV ±1 and CAP ±1 sensitivity gives BQS 5.00–5.64; CAP ±1 gives GQS 6.45–6.75. These narrow changes do not cure the cash-reliability hold or establish a precise rank. [E02–E17]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Kaka makes PVC profiles, WPC profiles and sheets, uPVC door/window profiles, roofing and laminate-related products. They compete with wood, plywood, aluminium and other materials in doors, furniture, partitions, cabinets and interior/exterior finishes. The annual report describes more than 2,000 SKUs; CRISIL describes over 450 dealers across 20 states and union territories. These are attributed business disclosures, not independently audited retention cohorts. FY26 exports of about ₹0.50 crore indicate an overwhelmingly domestic business.

Profit depends on resin conversion, product mix, manufacturing yield, dealer reach and asset utilization. Integrated compounding/extrusion and captive power can reduce cost, but neither guarantees a selling-price premium. CRISIL describes customer credit of up to 50 days. Inventory, receivables and new equipment consume cash before profits become distributable.

The issuer also purchases stock in trade. Sales must therefore not be divided by nameplate capacity and called actual manufacturing utilization. Complete current product-wise tonnes, realized prices, manufacturing/trading mix and customer concentration were not located. This prevents a precise price/volume bridge, but does not negate audited sales growth or the independent rating's volume/dealer explanation. [E02,E05,E10,E11]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
MOAT 5 recognizes a useful but contestable manufacturing/distribution position. Product breadth, dealer relationships, local delivery and integrated facilities can improve service and cost. The evidence does not demonstrate persistent premium pricing, patented technology, dominant share or customer switching costs sufficient for a high moat score. Resin inputs and competing product substitutions make this a competitive converter rather than a protected concession.

Official product sources establish three relevant competitive reference points. Dhabriya Polywood offers PVC/uPVC/WPC-related products and is the closest broad product-overlap reference. Fenesta competes in branded windows and doors with consultation, customization and installation, but is a group business division rather than a clean standalone valuation peer. Rushil Decor's laminate/MDF and VIR PVC offering overlaps in building-material demand but has a different manufacturing and commodity mix.

These comparisons explain competitive threats and business-model differences; they are not a matched valuation table. No unsupported peer P/E median, relative-value discount, or market-share ranking is used. A credible moat upgrade would require repeat orders, dealer productivity, sustained gross margins through resin cycles and return premiums not explained merely by capacity expansion. [E05,E10,E11,E15]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable standalone sales rose from ₹78.7489 crore in FY21 to ₹116.9592 crore in FY22, ₹153.9347 crore in FY23, ₹170.2163 crore in FY24, ₹197.7834 crore in FY25 and ₹263.2330 crore in FY26. Six observations support the preferred five-year CAGR of 27.30%; the three-year CAGR is 19.58%. FY26 growth was 33.09%. FY21 was pandemic-affected, and exact price/volume separation is incomplete, so the measurement does not imply a pure volume CAGR.

Economic cross-checks are favorable: prospectus output rose from 8,692 tonnes in FY21 to 10,931 in FY22 and 11,968 in FY23; Lasundra moved from phased operations to fuller integration; CRISIL attributes recent growth to higher volumes and wider dealer access. Its August rationale reports roughly ₹76 crore revenue in Q1 FY27. This is a dated rating disclosure, not a complete audited quarter or a reason to annualize one quarter into a forecast. Comparable current interim cash flow and a full audited TTM remain ND.

REV 8 follows the 20–30% five-year CAGR band. No net trajectory uplift is applied: recent acceleration is positive but three-year growth is lower, and Medium confidence caps the score at 8. The temporary FY23 JV consolidation is removed before growth calculation, not penalized again. [E02,E05,E10,E11]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
DUR 6 reflects accessible domestic substitution demand and existing distribution, balanced against construction cycles and competitive access. Finished-product nameplate capacity is 59,576 tonnes per year: PVC 32,493, WPC 14,736, roofing/other products 6,410, uPVC 3,537 and laminate 2,400. Intermediate compounding capacity of 14,515 tonnes is deliberately excluded from this sum to avoid double counting. Current actual production and utilization remain ND. Model capacity equivalents use an explicitly illustrative ₹1 lakh per tonne, not an asserted realization.

CAP 5 is supported by a stable organic multi-year bridge, not current ROCE alone. Operating assets and liabilities reconcile FY21 operating capital of ₹27.9972 crore after unpaid operating expenses to the ₹27.3101 crore funding proxy after deferred tax and employee/tax provisions. FY26 operating capital after operating bonus is ₹179.6706 crore; deducting capital creditors, accrued interest, tax, gratuity and deferred tax reconciles to ₹174.4758 crore. Identified restricted current deposits of ₹2.4278 crore are added back for the operating-capital measure, giving ₹182.0984 crore. The ₹0.0345 crore noncurrent deposit is already inside other noncurrent assets and is not added twice. Nonoperating investments/property of ₹3.5273 crore are excluded.

The five-year increase in normalized NOPAT is ₹18.74985 crore against ₹154.1012 crore additional operating capital, or 12.17%. Funding proxies give 12.74% over five years and 11.16% over three. These are mixed returns around a reasoned 12–15% capital-cost range, not proven project IRRs. Early capital-creditor splits and immature assets limit precision. Solar's claimed ₹0.35–0.40 crore monthly saving on approximately ₹25.48 crore March project CWIP is gross power saving, not after-tax return after rent, maintenance, reinvestment and finance costs. [E03,E06,E10,E11]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Management delivered meaningful capacity expansion and a subsequent sales/PAT ramp. Lasundra phased operations in FY24 became fully integrated by FY26; the 7.5 MW solar project commissioned in mid-June 2026 after the January rating described its financing plan. EXEC 7 recognizes delivered assets and operations, not yet-verified solar economics or proposed exchange migration.

GOV 4 reflects material, specific weaknesses. The July 2023 prospectus disclosed 2018 promoter/group tax searches, 2021 settlement applications admitting additional income, the tax authority's July 2022 completeness objection, and January 2023 replies. The listed issuer was incorporated in 2019 and was not impleaded. No later final settlement order was located. This report neither assigns promoter liabilities to the issuer nor asserts that old proceedings are definitely still pending today.

FY26 secretarial findings include retrospective structured-digital-database entries and delayed credit-rating and 2 January board-outcome disclosures. Management attributes these to operational oversight and reports stronger controls; the response is preserved, but future compliance has not independently demonstrated remediation. Directors received ₹1.80 crore aggregate remuneration, around 9.6% of PAT, and disclosed related-party rent was ₹0.69 crore. Promoter demand loans were ₹6.3692 crore. Commercial leases and loans are not proof of abuse, but dependence on related-party operating and solar land matters.

Counterevidence is substantial: the main audit is unmodified, the audit trail operated throughout with no observed tampering, and the separate IFC opinion says controls were adequate and operating effectively at March-end. CARO reports no observed fraud, borrowing default or wilful default. These findings prevent an unsupported severe-governance conclusion; they do not erase the specific secretarial and cash-classification issues. [E07–E10,E17]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBITDA is ₹35.4008 crore after excluding all other income, versus management's approximately ₹35.99 crore measure including it. Operating EBIT is ₹30.6942 crore after also removing ₹0.0155 crore investment-property depreciation; operating D&A is ₹4.7066 crore. Thus property income and depreciation are both outside operating earnings when property is separately valued. Expensed finance cost is ₹6.3733 crore; capitalized interest of ₹0.3315 crore is separately disclosed. Operating EBIT interest coverage is about 4.82×. Using ₹6.341 crore cash/current accounts, net debt/operating EBITDA is about 2.75×.

Reported CFO/PAT is 0.7084 over FY24–26 and 0.5790 over six years. Three-year reported CFO less cash operating capex totals negative ₹69.4856 crore. Capex itself does not reduce CFO, but capital creditors affect its classification: balances were ₹1.2478/5.7394/0.7975 crore in FY24/25/26. Removing the FY25 creditor increase of ₹4.4916 crore gives operating CFO negative ₹0.6297 crore before financing interest; adding back the FY26 creditor repayment of ₹4.9419 crore gives ₹20.8155 crore. Move equal amounts to investing, preserving total cash and avoiding double deduction. A full earlier adjusted series remains unavailable.

Explained comparability changes are not misconduct: FY24 credit-card payables of ₹0.9098 crore moved into borrowing, and ₹0.5917 crore expense provisions moved into current liabilities. FY25 comparative CFO and cash capex both increased ₹0.0221 crore, preserving FCF and net cash. However, FY26 note 13 describes a ₹2.9028 crore noncash property transfer while CFI labels it a purchase. PPE gross deductions of ₹3.1413 crore equal land ₹0.9330, building ₹1.9698 and plant ₹0.2384. Plant net disposal value ₹0.1773 less loss ₹0.0107 gives ordinary proceeds ₹0.1666; adding the land transfer exactly explains reported proceeds ₹1.0996. This narrows the issue to classification, not an unexplained extra cash receipt. A complete gross capex/noncash reconciliation is still needed. Noncurrent-asset cash-flow receipt ₹0.2256 also approximates deposit release ₹0.2100 plus property depreciation ₹0.0156, another classification cross-check rather than proven cash loss.

The full CARO bank reconciliation is embedded; signs mean books minus statements filed with banks. The largest inventory difference is negative ₹0.3975 crore in September; March is positive ₹0.2178 crore. Receivable differences are small; payable differences range from negative ₹0.3338 to positive ₹0.3094 crore. Management cites provisional inventory valuation and account reconciliations. They are preserved alongside the favorable audit-trail and IFC opinions, not characterized as fraud.

FY26 inventory of ₹47.4625 crore and net receivables of ₹34.9822 crore grew slower than sales, a positive. Good receivables older than six months are ₹1.3976 crore; doubtful ₹1.1157 crore is fully provided. Bad-debt/provision expense was ₹1.5188 crore. Net average receivable days are approximately 43.6 using total sales as a credit-sales proxy. Reported cash ₹8.7688 crore includes restricted deposits; audited cash/current accounts ₹6.341 crore differ from CRISIL's approximate ₹2 crore unencumbered description. No restriction on all current accounts is inferred. [E03,E04,E06,E09,E16,E17]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated price times 13,660,000 shares gives market value ₹294.6462 crore, historical P/E 15.69× and P/B 3.54×. A March-balance cross-check adds debt and long gratuity and subtracts cash/current accounts and separately valued nonoperating assets, producing EV ₹388.9808 crore or 10.99× operating EBITDA. It is not a current October enterprise value. Operating properties receive no extra value; operating rents stay expensed rather than also capitalizing lease debt. Investment property is valued at net book only, with its income/depreciation excluded from operating earnings.

The linked model begins with a March-to-October pre-entry bridge, then the remaining FY27 stub, full FY28–31 and 202/366 of FY32 through 19 October 2031. It models revenue, margins, D&A, cash taxes, working capital, capex, principal, average-balance interest, cash, debt and shares in each period. Interest, cash tax and incremental CC draw are solved simultaneously. March CARO sanctioned CC limits total ₹57 crore against ₹38.1135 crore draw, permitting at most ₹18.8865 crore additional existing-facility draw. This is not new equity rescue and not an unlimited plug. Availability/renewal is conditional. ₹2 crore initial available cash and required reserve are conservative; a ₹6.341 crore cash sensitivity is separate.

Opening capital creditors ₹0.7975 crore, tax ₹0.3822 crore, current gratuity ₹0.1393 crore, accrued interest ₹0.1716 crore and bonus ₹0.2853 crore are paid once. Future normal bonus expense/cash sits inside margins. Long gratuity ₹0.5488 crore remains a terminal and DCF claim. Capital commitment ₹0.9293 crore is included within FY27 capex, not added twice; ₹3.1283 crore bank guarantees are contingent, not automatic cash payments. Base revenue growth fades from 20% to 8%, EBITDA margin is 14–14.5%, operating NWC is 27–26% of sales, capex ₹8–12 crore and terminal EV/EBITDA 10×. Bear margins are 10.5–12% with slower collections and 7× exit; bull growth/margins/capex are explicitly higher with 12× exit. These are analyst assumptions, not guidance.

Conditional base/bull are funded and return 21.87%/35.59% per year. Bear no-rescue return is null after a ₹6.5128 crore cash-floor gap. A separate counterfactual upfront bear rescue at 30% discount and 3% fees raises gross ₹6.7143 crore, net ₹6.5128 crore, issues 444,683 shares and dilutes existing ownership 3.15%, distinct from 3.26% share-count expansion. Its return is -6.86%, not an entry target or available financing. Base/bull need no rescue.

Ordinary returns and all ordinary entry prices remain null. The conditional reverse solver brackets 15% return at 8.3–8.4% constant growth, with both endpoints funded under base margins, capex and 10× exit; this is not an ordinary solved growth requirement. DCF uses 12/14/16% WACC, 3/4/5% terminal growth and 14% terminal ROIC with reinvestment and cash-reserve growth. Signed modeled entry cash minus reserves is retained. DCF terminal-value shares, 12/15/18% equity hurdle entries, working-capital/margin/capex/rate/facility stresses and execution-cost/dilution grids are embedded. [E03,E04,E05,E13,E14,E17]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that a price-sensitive converter installs assets faster than it generates durable owner cash. Resin competition or weaker construction demand reduces margins while dealer collections slow and inventory remains elevated. Principal repayments continue, collateral is pledged and related-party land dependence does not create separately realizable operating-property value. Useful solar and capacity assets can still coexist with adverse minority recapitalization.

The linked bear combines a 5% initial sales decline, 10.5% EBITDA margin and operating NWC at 33% of sales, followed by modest recovery. Even with documented existing-facility headroom it has a ₹6.51 crore funding gap. The separate discounted rescue leaves terminal price about ₹151.18, roughly 30% below reference, or -6.86% annualized. Unavailable rescue could be materially worse. In base sensitivities, five extra working-capital points create a ₹9.25 crore gap; two points less margin create ₹0.83 crore; combined weaker margin/collections, 50% higher capex and two-point higher interest create ₹37.31 crore. These are hypothetical linked stresses, not evidence of actual default.

Counterevidence is meaningful: CRISIL reaffirmed BBB/Stable with adequate liquidity in August; bank limits are documented; capacity is delivered; FY26 earnings improved; stock and receivables grew slower than sales; doubtful debt is provided. Lower discretionary growth capex, verified headroom and better collections could improve resilience. D 3 reflects material impairment/recapitalization exposure under stress, not a claim that the base is currently insolvent. Permanent-loss risk is High, driven by recurring cash after necessary reinvestment versus debt service rather than ordinary quoted volatility. [E03,E05,E14,E16,E17]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold or tenfold share-price outcome in five years requires 37.97% or 58.49% annual compounding. At unchanged shares, 15× terminal P/E and 7% net margin, the algebra requires roughly ₹1403 crore or ₹2806 crore terminal sales, compared with ₹263.233 crore in FY26. These are requirements, not forecasts. A lower terminal multiple or dilution increases the necessary earnings; a higher margin lowers required sales but needs economic support.

At an explicitly illustrative ₹1 lakh revenue per tonne, the fivefold requirement is about 140,000 tonnes, more than twice disclosed finished-product nameplate. Product mix and traded goods could change this conversion, but neither is assumed to create costless scale. New capacity would require capex, working capital, distribution access and demonstrated incremental returns. The current bull model already retains higher capex rather than treating expansion as free.

Classification: speculative/unsupported on current evidence, not mathematically impossible. Better utilization, cash realization and after-tax returns on the new assets are more decision-relevant than a multibagger label. The requirements should be rerun after any new equity issuance; share-count expansion and existing-holder dilution must not be confused. [E06,E11,E14]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor the variables that can change the conclusion, not just the share price:
1. Obtain an auditor-supported property-transfer, gross capex/disposal and capital-creditor cash bridge. Baselines are ₹2.9028 crore property transfer and FY25/26 capital-creditor changes of +₹4.4916/−₹4.9419 crore. A coherent reconciliation can clear G2; continued material unexplained classification keeps it open.
2. Reconcile unrestricted cash and facilities against obligations. March cash/current accounts are ₹6.341 crore versus the rating's approximately ₹2 crore unencumbered cash; March sanctioned CC is ₹57 crore, August rated CC ₹57.68 crore and average usage 83%. Near-full usage with persistent deficits is an alert; inability to service obligations is thesis-breaking.
3. Track operating CFO excluding capital-creditor financing and after interest, together with essential capex. Persistent negative owner cash after major projects complete weakens the growth thesis.
4. Require actual finished tonnes, utilization, realizations and manufacturing/trading mix. Nameplate capacity of 59,576 tonnes is not output or demand.
5. Compare realized solar savings with ₹0.35–0.40 crore per month after lease, maintenance, tax and debt service; gross savings alone do not demonstrate CAP improvement.
6. Track inventory and receivable ageing: ₹47.4625 crore stock, ₹1.3976 crore good receivables older than six months and ₹1.1157 crore doubtful receivables already provided. Unprovided losses or repeated growth well above sales require investigation.
7. Seek final historical promoter/group tax outcomes and verify real-time SDD/disclosure compliance rather than accepting remediation claims indefinitely. Track recurring CARO bank reconciliation differences and IFC/audit-trail changes.
8. Review related-party land rent, remuneration and promoter-loan withdrawals or fresh funding on economic terms.
9. Verify postal-ballot outcome and actual exchange approvals before crediting migration with better liquidity.
10. Before implementation, refresh BSE lot size, restrictions, official trading calendar/turnover and live depth for the actual position. This is a research checklist, not a recurring service or trading instruction. [E01–E17]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Kaka is a leveraged capacity-ramp manufacturer with genuine expansion and mixed business quality. BQS 5.32 and GQS 6.60 summarize historical evidence, but numerical ranking eligibility is withheld while G2 cash classification remains materially unresolved. IAS is NS because R, P and L cannot support ordinary investment conclusions. No governance or funding-failure cap is applied, and no overall point is invented.

Action category: research priority / wait for evidence. Resolve cash classifications and current resource definitions, then rerun the funded per-share model at a verified executable price. The positive conditional base is worth investigating; it is not discarded merely because a bear gap exists. Conversely, the rescue-only case is not an investable target. The distinction between conditional operating upside and verified financeability is essential.

The ₹5 lakh illustration is not a suggested allocation. At ₹215.70, one 500-share lot costs ₹107,850; four lots are ₹431,400 and five ₹539,250. Secondary volume proxies imply around 6.4 days at 5% participation before whole-lot constraints, but median whole-lot capacity at that rate is zero. Thus fractional participation arithmetic does not promise an executable exit. Existing-holder decisions would require actual quantity, taxes and portfolio exposure, none supplied. A price fall or main-board migration alone would not cure cash classification or improve incremental capital returns. [E03–E17]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Core factual sources are the July 2023 final prospectus, FY24–26 audited annual reports, October 2026 postal ballot, dated CRISIL rationales and the official interoperable security master. Exact exchange filing identifiers are retained where a public Business Standard mirror supplied the document. The original issuer/exchange files were not silently substituted with an aggregator's financial table. Rating opinions supply independent credit context, not guaranteed cash availability. Secondary OHLCV is explicitly labeled; 21 October observations are excluded from the price/liquidity cutoff. Undated/current peer product pages establish product context only, not contemporaneous historical valuation multiples.

Source URLs, document dates, locators and original SHA-256 hashes accompany financial-only extracts. The canonical record embeds all historical financials, annual funding/valuation rows, scenarios, sensitivities, score contributions, audit findings and limitations. Analytical backups contain the safe extracts and reproducible calculations, not original PDFs, raw HTML/OCR, images, personal identifiers or shareholder lists. Source-free reproduction verifies calculations; fresh authentication requires retrieving cited documents and comparing source hashes.

Open questions remain: complete property/capex cash classification; older capital-creditor baselines; cash definition and current facility availability; full current volumes/prices/customer concentration; project returns after all costs; final historical promoter tax outcomes; demonstrated control remediation; actual migration approval; complete official BSE turnover/calendar and current restrictions. Model growth, margins, working capital, capex, tax, interest, reserve cash, terminal multiples and recapitalization terms are assumptions, not facts. This report is research, not personalized investment advice, a live quotation or an instruction to transact.

financial_reconciliations.detail: Prospectus FY23 consolidated revenue 158.4989 and PAT 7.1850 include one-year Shri Rang Energy Efficient JV. FY24 audited comparative standalone revenue 153.9347, PAT 7.2039 and CFO 8.4833 are used throughout. JV exit 1 April 2023; no subsidiary/JV in FY26.

FY25 note reclassifies 0.9098 crore credit-card payables from trade payable to short-term borrowing, and 0.5917 short-term provisions to other current liabilities. Latest comparable debt 45.5652 adopted, not original 44.6554.
FY26 adds 0.0221 crore asset disposal loss to FY25 CFO and cash capex: CFO 3.8398 to 3.8619, capex 26.1515 to 26.1736, preserving net cash and FCF.

Cash-flow trade-payable movements closely track total payables, which include capital creditors. FY25 creditor increase 4.4916 and FY26 decline 4.9419 must be removed from operating conversion and moved to investing when preparing an adjusted view. FY23 capital-creditor baseline unavailable.

FY26 note 13 describes a noncash property transfer of 2.9028 crore, whereas CFI labels it purchase. Ordinary disposal NBV 0.1773 less loss 0.0107 gives proceeds 0.1666; plus land transfer 0.9330 exactly equals reported PPE proceeds 1.0996. Thus the excess is arithmetically classified, not an unexplained cash receipt. A full gross capex/noncash bridge remains necessary; no cash loss or fraud is inferred.
Audited 6.341 cash/current accounts versus rating approximate 2 unencumbered at March; preserve discrepancy and do not infer a current bank draw from average utilisation.
